question: Which accepted public-contract boundary should own relationally invalid resource manifests, given that accepted H1 constructors and strict deserialization reject duplicate resource IDs/paths and self-dependencies before a ResourceManifest exists, while accepted H1 action semantics and accepted H3 resolution oracles require ValidateResourceManifest to receive those states and emit PIH.RESOURCE.DUPLICATE_ID, DUPLICATE_PATH, and OVERLAY_REPLACEMENT?

options.summary: Authorize a bounded upstream H1/H3 contract correction that moves the affected manifest relational invalidity to ValidateResourceManifest.
options.consequence: Keep H2 blocked. Explicitly revise the accepted constructor/wire/schema boundary so relationally invalid but structurally representable manifests can reach ValidateResourceManifest, reconcile the affected H1 invariant/version rules and H3 schemas/fixtures/oracles, independently review that upstream correction, and resume H2 only under a separately recorded bounded authorization. No H4 or other successor activates.

options.summary: Preserve strict H1 constructors/deserialization and revise the conflicting H1 action-code ownership and H3 action oracles.
options.consequence: Keep H2 blocked. Treat duplicate/self-dependent manifest inputs as PIH.WIRE.INVALID_VALUE with no ResourceManifest, remove or reassign unreachable action expectations, reconcile accepted H1/H3 evidence and versions under explicit authority, and resume H2 only after independent review. No H4 or other successor activates.

options.summary: Reject both corrections and reopen the broader version-1 manifest-validation contract.
options.consequence: Keep H2 blocked and reopen only the human-specified manifest construction, deserialization, schema, issue-code, and action boundary. No implementation correction or successor work resumes until a replacement contract is accepted.

Retain the provisional H2 implementation, tests, reviews, and failed correction evidence without commit/push or final H2 acceptance. H2 remains blocked; H4, H5, P2, project-local cutover, SQLite, protected execution, and scientific execution remain unstarted.

recommendation: Option A. It preserves the accepted purpose of ValidateResourceManifest and the DataObject/ActionObject rule that cross-resource duplicate, overlay, and dependency relations belong to the ActionObject. Because H1 and H3 are already human-accepted, this must be an explicit bounded upstream contract/resource correction with version-boundary reconciliation, not an H2 implementation guess.
blocked_scope: H2 completion, further writer/reviewer loops, final H2 acceptance checkpoint, commit/push of the H2 boundary, H4/H5/P2 activation, project-local Python/cutover, accepted H3 mutation, SQLite, live-skill retirement, dependencies/lockfiles, protected/external/numerical/scientific/release/publication execution, and unrelated user work.
safe_scope: Read-only inspection of H1 field/wire/action/version contracts, accepted H3 schemas and resource-resolution fixtures/oracles, provisional H2 source/tests/docs, initial reviews, the single correction-cycle record, validation evidence, and this checkpoint. The resolve-human-checkpoint procedure may record an unambiguous human choice and authorize only its bounded upstream correction/resumption scope.
